subject: Post-demo: recommended inference trio + regression guardrails

Subject: Post-demo: recommended inference trio + regression guardrails

Alex — great to meet today. Quick recap from our demo and a recommended, operationally-focused shortlist so your engineers and procurement can move forward: 

TL;DR (recommended trio)
- Redwood-Instruct-13B (fp16) — best balance: strong instruction-following, predictable tail latency at 100–200 tokens, good cost profile for batch sizes >4.
- OpenFT-7B-Q8 — lowest cost per token for light-weight UIs and high QPS; expect slightly reduced recall on long-context QA.
- Llama2-70B-8bit (quant) — highest quality for complex extraction and reasoning; higher baseline latency and infra cost but fewer model mistakes for your financial reconciliation flows.

Why these three? We mapped your target workloads (search-ranking + reconciliation assistant + short-form customer replies) to models with different cost/latency/quality sweet spots and built a fallback policy so you can meet availability SLOs. I've attached a one-pager that summarizes throughput/lab benchmarks and a sample prompt set we ran against your anonymized transcripts.

Benchmarks and artifacts attached/linked:
- benchmark CSV (benchmarks_q8_fp16.csv) — token-level latency and cost for 4 common request patterns.
- prompt set (cloudora_prompt_set_v1.json) — canonical prompts we recommend locking for regression tests.
- short one-pager (redwood_shortlist_onepager.pdf) — executive view for procurement.

Operational notes / risks:
- Cold-start tail on the 70B quantized run is ~210–250ms extra for single-stream requests; we'll recommend warm-pooling for your realtime path.
- OpenFT-7B-Q8 requires careful prompt anchoring to avoid hallucinations on reconciliation prompts; we recommend a short QA filter step to flag low-confidence generations.
- Regression risk: switching from the 13B fp16 to the 7B Q8 for cost reasons produced a 4–6% drop on our precision@k tests for your prompt set in our baseline evaluation. We can mitigate via prompt tuning and prefix caching.

Next asks (proposed):
1) Confirm target 95th-pct latency for interactive flows (is 350ms an acceptable SLO?)
2) Confirm target sustained throughput (you mentioned ~120 rps during peak; please confirm burst expectations)
3) Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive for your infra/ML teams next week (we can run live benchmarks with your sample dataset)

If useful I can also prepare an ops runbook for canarying the 70B fallback in Dedicated or Private deployment (includes cache sizing, batching guidance, and automatic fallback rules).

Thanks — Ill wait for the throughput/latency answers and will book the deep-dive once we sync on a slot.

—Kim

Adding a few concrete operational data points to Alexs questions: 

- 13B (fp16) latency: our internal single-stream p95 numbers on A100-ish hardware are ~260–320ms at batch=1 depending on token length; at batch=4 we see p95 ~140–180ms. For your expected prompt lengths (~60–120 tokens) plan on ~300ms p95 without warm pools.
- OpenFT-7B-Q8 cost: roughly 35–45% lower per-token than 13B fp16 in our current pricing model given identical batching; approximate per-1M-token cost: 
  * Redwood-Instruct-13B (fp16) — $95–$120 per 1M tokens (estimate, depends on batching & KV cache hit rate)
  * OpenFT-7B-Q8 — $45–$70 per 1M tokens
  * Llama2-70B-8bit (quant) — $320–$420 per 1M tokens (higher but fewer downstream RTOs on complex tasks)

- Regression mitigation: the 4–6% precision drop I mentioned is on our baseline after a single-pass prompt tuning we ran in-house. Deeper prompt tuning + a light calibration layer (classifier to filter low-confidence responses) typically brings most customers within 1–2% of the fp16 baseline. Typical tuning cadence: 2–3 sprints (2–4 weeks total) depending on lab access & annotation velocity.

Operational recommendations: 
- Start pilot with 13B fp16 for interactive user paths (meets 300ms p95 with warm pools), and route high-precision reconciliation tasks to the 70B quant. Use 7B-Q8 for low-cost background async replies and non-critical scales.
- Enable KV prefix caching for the reconciliation pipeline to reduce repeated prompt costs.
- Instrument prompt-level quality metrics and fail-open to the higher-quality model if confidence falls below threshold.

Attached: quick benchmark CSV and a short runbook (see redwood_shortlist_onepager.pdf and benchmarks_q8_fp16.csv in Kims original). Happy to present these numbers in the technical deep-dive.

—Karthik
